title: Dynamic Trace Export Switchboard for Tiered Backends
creator: Marcus Li
description: Build a tenant-aware export switchboard that routes OTLP traces to a tiered set of backends with graceful degradation. Goal: support per-tenant backend priority lists, on-the-fly failover to secondary vendors (Tempo/Jaeger-compatible endpoints), adaptive batching per backend, and lightweight transform hooks for field normalization and PII redaction before export. This will replace ad-hoc routing logic in the collector and centralize routing decisions in a single, observable component. The switchboard must preserve trace ordering guarantees for single-request flows, maintain idempotency for retried exports, and expose per-tenant drop metrics and SLA telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema supports per-tenant ordered backend lists and weight-based routing
Automatic failover to next available backend within 200ms on persistent error conditions
End-to-end integration test with Tempo and Jaeger test endpoints that validates span integrity and timing under failover
Observed tail latency for steady-state export remains < 100ms P95 for control traffic after switchboard enabled
Backpressure behavior documented and enforced: when all backends unhealthy, exporter responds with 429 and queues to durable buffer with bounded retention
Migration plan & canary rollout steps documented with rollback playbook
design_notes: Routing plane: in-memory priority map built from config service + on-demand resolution for new tenants
Transport: use OTLP/gRPC outbound for primary backends; fall back to HTTP/JSON envelope for legacy Jaeger endpoints
Enrichment: plugin hook chain to run deterministic field normalization, span attribute remapping, and tenant-level sampling hints
Batching: dynamic batch sizing based on backend health and observed ack latency; larger batches to slower backends to improve throughput
Backpressure: token-bucket per-backend with circuit-breaker that exposes health to router; when tripped, routing moves to next backend and emits metric
Durability: bounded local disk buffer (configurable size) with TTL for replay; plan for S3 archival for longer retention as follow-up
Security: mTLS to Tempo/Jaeger vendors where supported; credential rotation via KMS-backed secret store and automated refresh
Compatibility: translator layer for jaeger v2 envelopes to OTLP to preserve tags and trace ids
